title: Proof
body_md:
We prove it by induction on $h$. We start with $h=1$, namely $r=3$. 
In this case, (iii) and (iv)  follow from Theorem \ref{thm:antonelli3}. Indeed, take $\mathcal{V}_3 = \xi \otimes \varphi^*(\mathcal H_3)$ so, 
by \eqref{eq:cojo0} and semi--continuity, one has 
$$h^j(X_e, \mathcal{U}_{3} \otimes \mathcal{U}_{3}^{\vee}) = h^j(X_e, \mathcal{V}_{3} \otimes \mathcal{V}_{3}^{\vee}) = h^j(\mathbb{F}_e, \mathcal{A}_{3} \otimes \mathcal{A}_{3}^{\vee}) = 0,\; 2 \leqslant j\leqslant 3,$$which proves (iii) for $h=1$; moreover, 
by stability and semi--continuity, one has $h^0(X_e, \mathcal{U}_{3} \otimes \mathcal{U}_{3}^{\vee}) = h^0(X_e, \mathcal{V}_{3} \otimes \mathcal{V}_{3}^{\vee}) = 1$, therefore from the vanishings above one has  
$$\chi(X_e, \mathcal{U}_{3} \otimes \mathcal{U}_{3}^{\vee}) = 1 - h^1(X_e, \mathcal{U}_{3} \otimes \mathcal{U}_{3}^{\vee})  = 1 - \dim (\mathcal M(3)) = 1 - 2 (6b_e - 9e - 4) = 1 + 2(4 + 9e - 6b_e),$$which also 
proves (iv) for $h=1$. 

As for (i), by semi--continuity, one has $$h^j (X_e, \mathcal{U}_3 \otimes \mathcal{U}^{\vee}_2) \leqslant h^j (X_e, \mathcal{V}_3 \otimes \mathcal{V}^{\vee}_2) \;\; {\rm and} \;\;  
h^j (X_e, \mathcal{U}_2 \otimes \mathcal{U}^{\vee}_3) \leqslant h^j (X_e, \mathcal{V}_2 \otimes \mathcal{V}^{\vee}_3),$$for any $0 \leqslant j \leqslant 3$, where 
$\mathcal{V}_2 = \mathcal{V}$ as in the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:rk 2 vctB e>0}, i.e. 
$\mathcal{V}_2 = \xi \otimes \varphi^*(\mathcal H)$, where $c_1(\mathcal H) = C_e + (b_e-e-2)f = {\mathcal O}_{\mathbb{F}_e}(1, b_e-e-2)$.  
From Leray's isomorphism, projection formula and invariance under twists, it follows that, for any $0 \leqslant j \leqslant 3$, one has  
$$h^j(X_e, \mathcal{V}_3 \otimes \mathcal{V}_2^{\vee}) = h^j(\mathbb{F}_e, \mathcal H_3 \otimes \mathcal H^{\vee}) = h^j(\mathbb{F}_e, \mathcal{A}_3 \otimes \mathcal H_1^{\vee})$$and 
$$h^j(X_e, \mathcal{V}_2 \otimes \mathcal{V}_3^{\vee}) = h^j(\mathbb{F}_e, \mathcal H \otimes \mathcal H_3^{\vee}) = h^j(\mathbb{F}_e, \mathcal H_1 \otimes \mathcal{A}_3^{\vee}),$$where 
$\mathcal{A}_3 = \mathcal H_3(c_1(\mathcal E_e))$ is the rank-3 vector bundle on $\mathbb{F}_e$ as in the proof of Theorem \ref{thm:antonelli3} whereas $\mathcal H_1= \mathcal H(c_1(\mathcal E_e))$ 
is the rank-2 vector bundle on $\mathbb{F}_e$ as in \eqref{extensionsuFe}, which are both Ulrich w.r.t. $c_1(\mathcal E_e) = {\mathcal O}_{\mathbb{F}_e}(3, b_e)$. Therefore, for 
dimension reasons, $h^3(\mathbb{F}_e, \mathcal{A}_3 \otimes \mathcal H_1^{\vee}) = h^3(\mathbb{F}_e, \mathcal H_1 \otimes \mathcal{A}_3^{\vee}) = 0$, which implies therefore 
$h^3 (X_e, \mathcal{U}_3 \otimes \mathcal{U}^{\vee}_2) = h^3(X_e, \mathcal{U}_2 \otimes \mathcal{U}^{\vee}_3) = 0$, as desired. 

To prove that  $h^2(\mathbb{F}_e, \mathcal{A}_3 \otimes \mathcal H_1^{\vee})=0$ recall that, from \cite[Prop.\;6.4]{ant}, $\mathcal{A}_3$ arises as the cokernel of a general injective vector bundle map of the form
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cojocaz}
0 \to \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(2, b_e - e -1)^{\oplus \gamma} \to \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(2, b_e - e)^{\oplus \delta} \oplus \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(3, b_e-1)^{\oplus \tau} \to \mathcal{A}_3 \to 0,
\end{equation}for suitable positive integers $\gamma,\;\delta,\,\tau$ as in \cite[Thm.\;4.1]{ant}, in our situation  one can see that  $\gamma=b_e-3e+3,\;\delta=b-3e,\,\tau=6$. Tensoring \eqref{eq:cojocaz} by $\mathcal H_1^{\vee}$ gives that 
$$h^2(\mathbb{F}_e, \mathcal{A}_3 \otimes \mathcal H_1^{\vee}) \leqslant \delta\,h^2(\mathbb{F}_e,  \mathcal H_1^{\vee} \otimes \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(2, b_e - e)) + \tau\,h^2(\mathbb{F}_e,  
\mathcal H_1^{\vee} \otimes \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(3, b_e - 1)),$$
therefore to prove that $ h^2(\mathbb{F}_e, \mathcal{A}_3 \otimes \mathcal H_1^{\vee}) =0$ 
it is enough to show that 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cojo4}
h^2(\mathbb{F}_e,  \mathcal H_1^{\vee} \otimes \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(2, b_e - e)) = h^2(\mathbb{F}_e,  \mathcal H_1^{\vee} \otimes \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(3, b_e - 1)) = 0.
\end{equation}
Taking into account that $\mathcal H_1$ is of rank 2, i.e. $\mathcal H^{\vee}_1 \cong \mathcal H_1 (- c_1(\mathcal H_1))$, where 
$c_1(\mathcal H_1) = C_e + (b_e - e - 2)f = \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(1, b_e - e -2)$, from \eqref{extensionsuFe} one has that $\mathcal H_1 (- c_1(\mathcal H_1))$ fits 
in 
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cojo3}
0 \to \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(2, e+1) \to \mathcal H_1 (- c_1(\mathcal H_1)) \to I_Z \otimes \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(3, b_e+1)\to 0,
\end{equation}where $Z \subset \mathbb{F}_e$ is a general zero-dimensional subscheme of $\mathbb{F}_e$ of length $\ell(Z) = 2b_e - 3e$. Thus,  from \eqref{eq:cojo3}, to prove 
\eqref{eq:cojo4}  it is enough to prove that

$$h^2(\mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(4, b_e+1)) = h^2(\mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(5, b_e+e)) = h^2(I_Z \otimes \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(5, 2b_e-e+1)) = h^2(I_Z \otimes \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(6, 2b_e))=0,$$
which trivially hold true from either Serre duality on $\mathbb{F}_e$ or from the use of the exact sequence 
$0 \to I_Z \to \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e} \to \mathcal O_Z \to 0$. This shows that $h^2(\mathbb{F}_e, \mathcal{A}_3 \otimes \mathcal H_1^{\vee})=0$. 

To prove instead that $h^2(\mathbb{F}_e, \mathcal H_1 \otimes \mathcal{A}_3^{\vee})=0$, one considers the dual exact sequence of \eqref{eq:cojocaz}, i.e. 
\[
0 \to \mathcal{A}_3^{\vee} \to \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(-2, - b_e + e)^{\oplus \delta} \oplus \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(-3, - b_e+1)^{\oplus \tau} \to \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(-2, - b_e + e + 1)^{\oplus \gamma}  \to 0,
\]and tensor it by $\mathcal H_1$, which gives
\begin{eqnarray*}
h^2(\mathbb{F}_e, \mathcal H_1 \otimes \mathcal{A}_3^{\vee}) \leqslant & \delta\,h^2(\mathcal H_1 \otimes \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(-2, -b_e + e)) + \tau\,
h^2(\mathcal H_1\otimes \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(-3, - b_e + 1)) + \\ 
& \gamma\,h^1(\mathcal H_1 \otimes \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(-2, -b_e + e +1)).
\end{eqnarray*} From \eqref{extensionsuFe}, it is enough to prove 
$$h^2(\mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(1, e-1)) = h^2(\mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}) = h^1 (\mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(1, e)) = 0,$$and 
$$h^2(I_Z \otimes \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(2, b_e-1)) = h^2(I_Z \otimes \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(1, b_e-e)) = h^1(I_Z \otimes \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(2, b_e)) =0.$$The vanishings 
of the $h^2$'s easily follow from the same reasoning as above; by Leray's isomorphism and projection formula one gets 
$h^1 (\mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(1, e)) = h^1(\mathbb{P}^1, \mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}(e) \oplus \mathcal O_{\mathbb P^1}) = 0$. At last, if we take into account that 
$Z$ is a zero-dimensional subscheme of length $\ell(Z) = 2b_e - 3e$ of general points on $\mathbb{F}_e$, then $Z$ imposes independent conditions on the linear system 
$|\mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(2, b_e)|$ on $\mathbb{F}_e$, which is of dimension $3 b_e - 3e + 2 > \ell(Z) = 2b_e - 3e$ since $b_e \geqslant 3e+2$ by \eqref{eq:rem:assAB}; 
this means that $h^1(I_Z \otimes \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(2, b_e)) = h^1(\mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(2, b_e))$ and the latter is zero by standard computations. This shows that 
$h^2(\mathbb{F}_e, \mathcal H_1 \otimes \mathcal{A}_3^{\vee})=0$, which concludes the proof of (i) for $h=1$. 


Finally, to prove (ii) for $h=1$, from invariance of $\chi$ in irreducible families and from above one has 
$$\chi(X_e, \mathcal{U}_3 \otimes \mathcal{U}_2^{\vee}) = \chi(X_e, \mathcal{V}_3 \otimes \mathcal{V}_2^{\vee}) = \chi(\mathbb{F}_e, \mathcal H_3 \otimes \mathcal H^{\vee}) = \chi(\mathbb{F}_e, \mathcal{A}_3 \otimes \mathcal H_1^{\vee})$$and 
$$\chi(X_e, \mathcal{U}_2 \otimes \mathcal{U}_3^{\vee}) =  \chi(X_e, \mathcal{V}_3 \otimes \mathcal{V}_2^{\vee}) = \chi(\mathbb{F}_e, \mathcal H \otimes \mathcal H_3^{\vee}) = \chi(\mathbb{F}_e, \mathcal H_1 \otimes \mathcal{A}_3^{\vee}).$$Since 
$\mathcal{A}_3$ and $\mathcal H_1$ are both Ulrich bundles w.r.t. $c_1(\mathcal E_e) = 3 C_e + b_e f= \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(3, b_e)$ on $\mathbb{F}_e$, let us consider 
the smooth projective model $(S, \mathcal O_S(1)) \cong (\mathbb{F}_e, \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(3, b_e))$, which is a surface, in a suitable projective space, of 
degree $d := \deg(S) = (c_1(\mathcal E_e))^2 = 6 b_e - 9e$. Thus, from \cite[Prop.\;2.12]{c-h-g-s}, one has 
$$\chi(\mathbb{F}_e, \mathcal{A}_3 \otimes \mathcal H_1^{\vee}) = 3 c_1(\mathcal H_1) \cdot K_S - c_1(\mathcal{A}_3) \cdot c_1(\mathcal H_1) + 6 (2d-2)$$and 
$$\chi(\mathbb{F}_e, \mathcal H_1 \otimes \mathcal{A}_3^{\vee}) = 2 c_1(\mathcal{A}_3) \cdot K_S - c_1(\mathcal{A}_3) \cdot c_1(\mathcal H_1) + 6 (2d-2),$$where 
$p_a(S) =1$ and $K_S = - 2 C_e - (e+2)f$. 
Using that $ c_1(\mathcal H_1) = 7 C_e + (3b_e - e - 2) f$ and $c_1(\mathcal{A}_3) = 12 C_e + (4b_e -3)f$, one gets
$$c_1(\mathcal{A}_3) \cdot c_1(\mathcal H_1) = 64b_e - 96 e - 45,\; c_1(\mathcal{A}_3) \cdot K_S = 12 e - 8b_e - 18,$$
$$c_1(\mathcal H_1) \cdot K_S = 9e - 6 b_e - 10, \; 6 (2d-2) = 12(d-1) = 72b_e - 108e -12;$$plugging these computations in the previous formulas, one gets 
$$\chi(\mathbb{F}_e, \mathcal{A}_3 \otimes \mathcal H_1^{\vee}) = 15 e - 10 b_e +3 \;\; {\rm and} \;\; \chi(\mathbb{F}_e, \mathcal H_1 \otimes \mathcal{A}_3^{\vee}) = 12 e - 8 b_e -3,$$which concludes the proof of 
(ii) for $h=1$. 


We now prove by induction that all statements hold true also for any integer $h \geqslant 2$. Assume therefore that they are satisfied for all positive integers $k$ such that 
$1 \leqslant k \leqslant h-1$. 


  (i) Let $j \in \{2,3\}$.  By specialization and  \eqref{eq:estensioneodd} tensored with  $ {\mathcal{U}_2}^{\vee}$, we have \color{black}
  \[ h^j(\mathcal{U}_{2h+1} \otimes {\mathcal{U}_2}^{\vee}) \leqslant h^j(\mathcal{F}_{2h+1}\otimes {\mathcal{U}_2}^{\vee}) \leqslant h^j(\mathcal{U}_2\otimes {\mathcal{U}_2}^{\vee}) + h^j(\mathcal{U}_{2h-1}\otimes {\mathcal{U}_2}^{\vee}),\]
  and the latter are $0$ by induction. Similarly, by specialization and using the dual of  \eqref{eq:estensioneodd} tensored with  $ {\mathcal{U}_2}$ we have
  \[ h^j(\mathcal{U}_2 \otimes {\mathcal{U}^{\vee}_{2h+1}}) \leqslant h^j(\mathcal{U}_2 \otimes {\mathcal{F}^{\vee}_{2h+1}}) \leqslant h^j(\mathcal{U}_2\otimes {\mathcal{U}_2}^{\vee}) + h^j(\mathcal{U}_2\otimes {\mathcal{U}^{\vee}_{2h-1}}),\] which are again $0$ by induction.

(ii) By specialization, \eqref{eq:estensioneodd}  tensored with  $ {\mathcal{U}_2}^{\vee}$ and induction we have 
\begin{eqnarray*}
  \chi(\mathcal{U}_{2h+1} \otimes {\mathcal{U}_2}^{\vee}) & = & \chi(\mathcal{F}_{2h+1}\otimes {\mathcal{U}_2}^{\vee}) = \chi(\mathcal{U}_2\otimes {\mathcal{U}_2}^{\vee}) + \chi(\mathcal{U}_{2h-1}\otimes {\mathcal{U}_2}^{\vee}) \\
  & =  & (4 + 9e - 6b_e) + (h-2)(4 + 9e - 6b_e) + (15 e - 10 b_e +3).
  \end{eqnarray*} 
	Likewise, by specialization, the dual of \eqref{eq:estensioneodd} and induction, we have 
	
	\begin{eqnarray*}
  \chi(\mathcal{U}_2 \otimes {\mathcal{U}}^{\vee}_{2h+1}) & = & \chi( \mathcal{U}_2 \otimes {\mathcal F}^{\vee}_{2h+1}) = \chi(\mathcal{U}_2\otimes {\mathcal{U}_2}^{\vee}) + 
	\chi(\mathcal{U}_2 \otimes {\mathcal{U}}^{\vee}_{2h-1}) \\
  & =  & (4 + 9e - 6b_e) + (h-2)(4 + 9e - 6b_e) + (12 e - 8 b_e -3).
  \end{eqnarray*} 
	
  (iii) Let $j = 2,3$; by specialization, \eqref{eq:estensioneodd} and its dual we have
  \begin{eqnarray*}
    h^j(\mathcal{U}_{2h+1} \otimes \mathcal{U}_{2h+1}^{\vee}) & \leqslant & h^j(\mathcal{F}_{2h+1} \otimes \mathcal{F}_{2h+1}^{\vee}) \leqslant \\
                              & \leqslant &   h^j(\mathcal{U}_2 \otimes \mathcal{F}_{2h+1}^{\vee})+ h^j(\mathcal{U}_{2h-1} \otimes \mathcal{F}_{2h+1}^{\vee}) \\
                        & \leqslant & h^j(\mathcal{U}_2 \otimes {\mathcal{U}_2}^{\vee})+h^j(\mathcal{U}_2 \otimes \mathcal{U}_{2h-1}^{\vee})+ \\
                        &  &    +   h^j(\mathcal{U}_{2h-1} \otimes {\mathcal{U}_2}^{\vee}) + h^j(\mathcal{U}_{2h-1} \otimes \mathcal{U}_{2h-1}^{\vee}),
    \end{eqnarray*}
which are all $0$ by induction. 

(iv) By specialization, \eqref{eq:estensioneodd} and its dual we have
  \begin{eqnarray*}
    \chi(\mathcal{U}_{2h+1} \otimes \mathcal{U}^{\vee}_{2h+1}) & = & \chi(\mathcal{F}_{2h+1} \otimes \mathcal{F}^{\vee}_{2h+1}) =
                                 \chi(\mathcal{U}_2 \otimes \mathcal{F}^{\vee}_{2h+1})+\chi(\mathcal{U}_{2h-1} \otimes \mathcal{F}^{\vee}_{2h+1}) \\
                   & = & \chi(\mathcal{U}_2 \otimes {\mathcal{U}_2}^{\vee})+\chi(\mathcal{U}_2 \otimes \mathcal{U}^{\vee}_{2h-1})+ \chi(\mathcal{U}_{2h-1} \otimes {\mathcal{U}_2}^{\vee}) + \chi(\mathcal{U}_{2h-1} \otimes \mathcal{U}^{\vee}_{2h-1}).
    \end{eqnarray*} By induction, this equals
    \begin{eqnarray*} 
	(4 + 9e - 6b_e) + (h-2)(4 + 9e - 6b_e)+ (h-2)(4 + 9e - 6b_e) + (27 e - 18 b_e) + 1 + \nonumber \\
	+ 9 (h-2) (3e - 2 b_e) + ((h-2)^2 + 2) (4 + 9e - 6 b_e) = \nonumber \\
		= 1 + 9(h-1) (3e - 2 b_e) + (4 + 9 e - 6 b_e) ( 1 + h-2 + h-2 + (h-2)^2 +2) = \nonumber \\	
	 = 1 + 9(h-1) (3e - 2b_e) + ((h-1)^2 + 2) (4 + 9e - 6 b_e).  \nonumber 	
	 \end{eqnarray*}

body_md:
\label{prop:h+1odd}
  For all integers $h \geqslant 1$ the scheme $\mathcal M (2h+1)$ is not empty
and its general member $[\mathcal{U}_{2h+1}] \in \mathcal M (2h+1)$ corresponds to a rank-$(2h+1)$ vector bundle $\mathcal{U}_{2h+1}$ which is Ulrich w.r.t. $\xi$ and which satisfies 
$$c_1(\mathcal{U}_{2h+1})= (2h+1) \xi+ \varphi^*\mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(3,b_e-3)) + \varphi^*\mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(h-1,(h-1) (b_e - e -2))$$and 
$h^j(\mathcal{U}_{2h+1} \otimes \mathcal{U}_{2h+1}^{\vee})=0$, $j=2,3$.

label: eq:dimextodd
title: Proof
body_md:
We prove this by induction on $h$, the case $h=1$ being satisfied by the choice of $\mathcal M (3)$ as in Theorem \ref{thm:antonelli3}. Therefore, let $h \geqslant 2$; for general $[\mathcal{U}_{2h-1}] \in
  \mathcal M (2h-1)$ and $[\mathcal{U}_2] \in
  \mathcal M (2)$, one has 
	\begin{eqnarray*}
	\dim ({\rm Ext}^1(\mathcal{U}_{2h-1},\mathcal{U}_2)) = h^1(\mathcal{U}_2 \otimes \mathcal{U}_{2h-1}^{\vee}).
	\end{eqnarray*}
	By Lemma \ref{lemma:induodd}-(i) we have that 
	$h^j(\mathcal{U}_2 \otimes \mathcal{U}_{2h-1}^{\vee}) = 0$, for $j=2,3$. Therefore 
	\begin{eqnarray*}
	\chi(\mathcal{U}_2 \otimes \mathcal{U}_{2h-1}^{\vee}) = h^0(\mathcal{U}_2 \otimes \mathcal{U}_{2h-1}^{\vee}) - h^1(\mathcal{U}_2 \otimes \mathcal{U}_{2h-1}^{\vee})
	\end{eqnarray*}
	so, by specialization and invariance of $\chi$ in irreducible families, we have
  \begin{eqnarray} \label{eq:dimextodd}
    \dim ({\rm Ext}^1(\mathcal{U}_{2h-1},\mathcal{U}_2)) & = & h^1(\mathcal{U}_2 \otimes \mathcal{U}_{2h-1}^{\vee})  \\ \nonumber
		                                 & = &  -\chi(\mathcal{U}_2 \otimes \mathcal{U}_{2h-1}^{\vee})+h^0(\mathcal{U}_2 \otimes \mathcal{U}_{2h-1}^{\vee}) \\ \nonumber
	                                   &\geqslant&  -\chi(\mathcal{U}_2 \otimes \mathcal{U}_{2h-1}^{\vee}) =  - \chi(\mathcal{U}_2 \otimes \mathcal{F}_{2h-1}^{\vee})  \\ \nonumber
																		 & = &  (h-2) (6b_e - 9e -4) + (8b_e - 12 e +3) >0,  \nonumber 
    \end{eqnarray} the latter equality following from Lemma \ref{lemma:induodd}-(ii) (with $h$ replaced by $h-1$) whereas the last strict inequality 
		following from $h \geqslant 2$ and $b_e \geqslant 3e +2$ by \eqref{eq:rem:assAB}. 
		
		The above computations prove that $\dim ({\rm Ext}^1(\mathcal{U}_{2h-1},\mathcal{U}_2)) >0$,  i.e. there exist non-trivial extensions as in 
		\eqref{eq:estensioneodd}, and that the scheme $\mathcal M (2h+1)^{\rm ext}$, and so also $\mathcal M (2h+1)$, is not empty.
		
		The members of $\mathcal M (2h+1)$ have rank $2h+1$ and first Chern class as in \eqref{eq:c1rcasoeodd}, since 
		$c_1 (\mathcal{U}_{2h+1}) = c_1(\mathcal{F}_{2h+1})$ being constant in $\mathcal M (2h+1)$. It is  immediate  that extensions of Ulrich bundles are still Ulrich, so the general member $[\mathcal{U}_{2h+1}] \in 
		\mathcal M(2h+1)$ corresponds to an Ulrich bundle w.r.t. $\xi$. It also satisfies 
$h^j(\mathcal{U}_{2h+1} \otimes \mathcal{U}_{2h+1}^{\vee})=0$ for $j=2,3$ by Lemma \ref{lemma:induodd}-(iii).

body_md:
\label{prop:h+1-IIodd} For all integers $h \geqslant 1$ the scheme $\mathcal M (2h+1)$ is not empty, generically smooth 
of dimension 
\begin{eqnarray*} \dim (\mathcal M(2h+1)) = ((h-1)^2 +2) (6b_e - 9e -4) + 9(h-1) (2b_e - 3e).
\end{eqnarray*}
Its general member corresponds to a slope-stable bundle $\mathcal{U}_{2h+1}$ 
whose slope w.r.t. $\xi$ is $$\mu(\mathcal{U}_{2h+1}) = 8b_e - k_e - 12 e -3.$$Furthermore, $\mathcal M (2h+1)$ properly contains the locally closed 
subscheme $\mathcal M (2h+1)^{\rm ext}$, namely $\dim(\mathcal M (2h+1)^{\rm ext}) < \dim(\mathcal M (2h+1))$.

title: Proof
body_md:
We prove this by induction on $h$, the case $h=1$ being satisfied by $\mathcal M(3)$ as in Theorem \ref{thm:antonelli3}, where in such a case $\mathcal M(3)^{\rm ext} = \emptyset$. 


Let therefore $h \geqslant 2$ and assume that we have proved the statement for all positive integers $k \leqslant h-1$;  we will prove it for $h$.

The slope of the members of  $\mathcal M (2)$ and $\mathcal M (2h-1)$ are both equal to $ 8b_e - k_e - 12 e -3$ as in \eqref{eq:slopercasoeodd}. Thus, by \cite[Lemma\;4.2]{c-h-g-s}, the general member $[\mathcal{F}_{2h+1}] \in \mathcal M (2h+1)^{\rm ext}$ (which is not empty by Proposition \ref{prop:h+1odd}) corresponds to a simple bundle. Hence, by semi-continuity, 
also the general member $[\mathcal{U}_{2h+1}]\in \mathcal M (2h+1)$ corresponds to a simple bundle which also satisfies $h^j(\mathcal{U}_{2h+1} \otimes \mathcal{U}^{\vee}_{2h+1})=0$, $j=2,3$, by Lemma \ref{lemma:induodd}-(iii).
 
Therefore  $\mathcal M (2h+1)$ is smooth at $[\mathcal{U}_{2h+1}]$ (see, e.g., \cite[Prop. 2.10]{c-h-g-s}) with
\begin{eqnarray} \label{eq:dimUh+1odd}
  \dim(\mathcal M (2h+1))&=&h^1(\mathcal{U}_{2h+1} \otimes \mathcal{U}^{\vee}_{2h+1})\\ \nonumber
 &=&-\chi(\mathcal{U}_{2h+1} \otimes \mathcal{U}^{\vee}_{2h+1})+h^0(\mathcal{U}_{2h+1} \otimes \mathcal{U}_{2h+1}^{\vee}) \\
\nonumber  
&=& ((h-1)^2 +2) (6b_e - 9e -4)+ 9(h-1) (2b_e - 3e), 
\end{eqnarray} using the facts that $h^0(\mathcal{U}_{2h+1} \otimes \mathcal{U}^{\vee}_{2h})=1$ as $\mathcal{U}_{2h+1}$ is simple, and the computation of 
$\chi(\mathcal{U}_{2h+1} \otimes \mathcal{U}^{\vee}_{2h+1})$ in Lemma \ref{lemma:induodd}-(iv). This proves that $\mathcal M(2h+1)$ is generically smooth of the stated dimension. 

Finally, we prove that $\mathcal{U}_{2h+1}$ general is slope--stable and that \linebreak $\dim(\mathcal M (2h+1)^{\rm ext}) < \dim(\mathcal M (2h+1))$.
 If $\mathcal{U}_{2h+1}$ general were not slope-stable then we could find a one-parameter family of bundles 
$\{\mathcal{U}_{2h+1}^{(t)}\}$ over the disc $\Delta$ such that $\mathcal{U}_{2h+1}^{(t)}$ is a general member of $\mathcal M (2h+1)$ for $t \neq 0$ and $\mathcal{U}_{2h+1}^{(0)}$ lies in $\mathcal M (2h+1)^{\rm ext}$, and such that we have a destabilizing sequence
\begin{equation} \label{eq:destat1odd} 
    0 \to \mathcal{D}^{(t)} \to \mathcal{U}_{2h+1}^{(t)} \to \mathcal{G}^{(t)} \to 0
  \end{equation} for $t \neq 0$, which we can take to be saturated, that is, such that $\mathcal{G}^{(t)}$ is torsion free, whence so that $\mathcal{D}^{(t)}$ and $\mathcal{G}^{(t)}$ are (Ulrich) vector bundles  
	(see \cite[Thm. 2.9]{c-h-g-s} or \cite[(3.2)]{b}). The limit of $\mathbb P(\mathcal{G}^{(t)}) \subset \mathbb P(\mathcal{U}_{2h+1}^{(t)})$ defines a subvariety of $\mathbb P(\mathcal{U}_{2h+1}^{(0)})$ of the same dimension as 
	$\mathbb P(\mathcal{G}^{(t)})$, whence a coherent sheaf $\mathcal{G}^{(0)}$ of rank ${\rm rk} (\mathcal{G}^{(t)})$ with a surjection $\mathcal{U}_{2h+1}^{(0)} \twoheadrightarrow \mathcal{G}^{(0)}$. 
	Denoting by $\mathcal{D}^{(0)}$ its kernel, we have ${\rm rk} (\mathcal{D}^{(0)})= {\rm rk} (\mathcal{D}^{(t)})$ and 
	$c_1(\mathcal{D}^{(0)})=c_1(\mathcal{D}^{(t)})$. Hence, \eqref{eq:destat1odd} specializes to a destabilizing sequence for $t=0$. 
	
Lemma \ref{lemma:uniquedest1odd} yields  that ${\mathcal{D}^{(0)}}^{\vee}$ (resp., ${\mathcal{G}^{(0)}}^{\vee}$) 
is the dual of a member of $\mathcal M (3)$ (resp., of $\mathcal M (2h+1)$). It follows that
${\mathcal{D}^{(t)}}^{\vee}$ (resp., ${\mathcal{G}^{(t)}}^{\vee}$)
is a deformation of the dual of a member of $\mathcal M (2))$ (resp., of $\mathcal M (2h+1)$), whence that ${\mathcal{D}^{(t)}}$ (resp., ${\mathcal{G}^{(t)}}$) is a deformation of a member of $\mathcal M (2)$ (resp., $\mathcal M (2h+1)$), as both are locally free. It follows that 
$[\mathcal{U}_{2h+1}^{(t)}] \in \mathcal M (2h+1)^{\rm ext}$ for $t \neq 0$. Thus,
\begin{equation} \label{eq:sonugualiodd}
  \mathcal M (2h+1)^{\rm ext}=\mathcal M (2h+1).
\end{equation}

On the other hand we have
\begin{equation} \label{eq:dimext2odd}
  \dim (\mathcal M (2h+1)^{\rm ext}) \leqslant \dim (\mathbb P({\rm Ext}^1(\mathcal{U}_{2h-1},\mathcal{U}_2))) +\dim (\mathcal M (2h-1)) +\dim (\mathcal M (2)),
\end{equation}
for $[\mathcal{U}_{2h-1}] \in \mathcal M (2h-1)$ and $[\mathcal{U}_2]\in \mathcal M (2)$ general.  Because  $\mathcal{U}_2$  is  slope--stable and also $\mathcal{U}_{2h-1}$  is slope--stable by induction, of the same slope,  we have 
$h^0(\mathcal{U}_2 \otimes \mathcal{U}_{2h-1}^{\vee})=0$. Thus, \eqref{eq:dimextodd} gives 
\[  h^1(\mathcal{U}_2 \otimes \mathcal{U}^{\vee}_{2h-1})  =  -\chi(\mathcal{U}_2 \otimes \mathcal{U}^{\vee}_{2h-1}) = (h-2) (6b_e - 9e -4) + (8b_e - 12e +3). 
\]Hence, from \eqref{eq:dimext2odd}, using also \eqref{eq:dimUh+1odd} and the fact that $\dim(\mathcal M(2)) = (6b_e - 9e -3)$ 
from Theorem \ref{thm:rk 2 vctB e>0}, one has 
\begin{eqnarray*}
  \dim (\mathcal M (2h+1)^{\rm ext}) & \leqslant & (h-2)(6b_e - 9e -4) + (8b_e - 12 e +3) - 1 + \\
	&  & + ((h-2)^2 + 2) (6b_e - 9e - 4) + 9 (h-2) (2b_e - 3e) +  (6b_e - 9e -3) \\
  & < & ((h-1)^2 +2)(6b_e - 9e -4)+ 9(h-1) (2b_e - 3e) =\dim (\mathcal M (2h+1)), 
\end{eqnarray*} as $h \geqslant 2$. The previous inequality shows that 
$\dim (\mathcal M (2h+1)^{\rm ext}) < \dim (\mathcal M (2h+1))$, as stated; in particular \eqref{eq:sonugualiodd} is a contradiction, 
which forces also $\mathcal{U}_{2h+1}$ general to be slope-stable.

body_md:
\label{thm:generale}  Let  $(X_e, \xi) \cong (\mathbb{ P}({\mathcal E_e}),{\mathcal O}_{\mathbb{P}({\mathcalE_e})}(1))$ be a $3$-fold  scroll over $\mathbb{F}_e$, with $e>0$ and $\mathcal E_e$ as in Assumptions \ref{ass:AB}. 
Let $\varphi: X_e \to \mathbb{F}_e$ be the scroll map and $F$ be the $\varphi$-fibre. Let $r \geqslant 2$ be any integer. 

Then the moduli space of rank-$r$ vector bundles $\mathcal{U}_r$ on $X_e$ which are Ulrich w.r.t. $\xi$ and with first Chern class
\begin{eqnarray*}c_1(\mathcal{U}_r) =
    \begin{cases}
      r \xi + \varphi^*\mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e} (3, b_e -3) + \varphi^*\mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}\left(\frac{r-3}{2}, \frac{(r-3)}{2} (b_e -  e- 2\right), & \mbox{if $r$ is odd}, \\
      r \xi + \varphi^*\mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}\left(\frac{r}{2}, \frac{r}{2}(b_e-e -2) \right), & \mbox{if $r$ is even}.
    \end{cases}\end{eqnarray*}
is not empty and it contains a generically smooth component $\mathcal M(r)$ of dimension 
		\begin{eqnarray*}\dim (\mathcal M(r) ) = \begin{cases} \left( \frac{(r-3)^2}{4} + 2 \right) (6 b_e - 9e -4) + \frac{9}{2} (r-3) (2b_e - 3e), & \mbox{if $r$ is odd}, \\
			 \frac{r^2}{4} (6b_e- 9e-4) +1 , & \mbox{if $r$ is even}.
    \end{cases}
    \end{eqnarray*} 
		The general member $[\mathcal{U}_r] \in \mathcal M(r)$  corresponds to a  slope-stable vector bundle, of slope w.r.t. $\xi$ given by 
$\mu(\mathcal{U}_r) = 8 b_e - k_e - 12 e - 3$.

body_md:
\label{thm:UlrichFe} For any integer $e \geqslant 0$, consider the Hirzebruch surface 
$\mathbb{F}_e$ and let $\mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(\alpha,\beta)$ denote the line bundle 
$\alpha C_e + \beta f$ on $\mathbb{F}_e$, where $C_e$ and $f$ are the generators 
of ${\rm Num}(\mathbb{F}_e)$.

Consider the very ample polarization $c_1(\mathcal{E}_e)= 3 C_e + b_e f$, where $b_e \geqslant 3e+2$. Then: 

\smallskip

\noindent 
(a) $\mathbb{F}_e$  does  not support any Ulrich line bundle  w.r.t. $c_1(\mathcal{E}_e)$ unless $e = 0$. In this latter case, the unique line bundles on 
$\mathbb{F}_0$ which are Ulrich w.r.t. $c_1(\mathcal{E}_e)$ are 
$$\mathcal L_1 :=\mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_0}(5,b_0-1) \; {\rm and} \; \mathcal L_2 := \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_0}(2,2b_0-1).$$  



\smallskip 

\noindent
(b) Set $e=0$ and let $r \geqslant2$ be any integer. Then the moduli space of rank-$r$ vector bundles $\mathcal{H}_r$ on $\mathbb{F}_0$ which are Ulrich w.r.t. $c_1(\mathcal{E}_0)$ and with first Chern class
\begin{eqnarray*}c_1(\mathcal{H}_r) =
    \begin{cases}
      \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_0}(3(r+1), (r+1) b_0 -3) \otimes  \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_0}\left(\frac{r-3}{2}, \frac{(r-3)}{2}(b_0-2)\right), & \mbox{if $r$ is odd}, \\
      \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_0}(3r, r b_0) \otimes \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_0}\left(\frac{r}{2}, \frac{r}{2}(b_0-2)\right), & \mbox{if $r$ is even}.
    \end{cases}\end{eqnarray*}
    is not empty and it contains a generically smooth component $\mathcal M_{\mathbb{F}_0}(r)$ of dimension 
		\begin{eqnarray*}\dim (\mathcal M_{\mathbb{F}_0}(r) ) = \begin{cases} \frac{(r^2 -1)}{4}(6 b_0 -4), & \mbox{if $r$ is odd}, \\
			 \frac{r^2}{4} (6b_0-4) +1 , & \mbox{if $r$ is even}.
    \end{cases}
    \end{eqnarray*}
    The general point $[\mathcal{H}_r] \in \mathcal M_{\mathbb{F}_0}(r)$ corresponds to a  slope-stable vector bundle.   


\smallskip 

 

\noindent
(c) When $e >0$, let $r \geqslant 2$ be any integer. Then the moduli space of rank-$r$ vector bundles $\mathcal{H}_{r}$ on $X_e$ which are Ulrich w.r.t. $c_1(\mathcal{E}_e)$ and with first Chern class
\begin{eqnarray*}c_1(\mathcal{H}_r) =
    \begin{cases}
     \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(3 (r+1), (r+1)b_e-3) \otimes \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}\left(\frac{r-3}{2}, \frac{(r-3)}{2}(b_e - e -2)\right), & \mbox{if $r$ is odd}, \\
      \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}(3 r, r b_e) \otimes  \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_e}\left(\frac{r}{2}, \frac{r}{2}(b_e-e-2)\right), & \mbox{if $r$ is even}.
    \end{cases}\end{eqnarray*}
    is not empty and it contains a generically smooth component $\mathcal M_{\mathbb{F}_e}(r)$ of dimension 
		\begin{eqnarray*}\dim (\mathcal M_{\mathbb{F}_e}(r) ) = \begin{cases} \left(\frac{(r -3)^2}{4}+ 2 \right)(6 b_e - 9e -4) + \frac{9}{2}(r-3) (2b_e-3e), & \mbox{if $r$ is odd}, \\
			 \frac{r^2}{4} (6b_e- 9e-4) +1 , & \mbox{if $r$ is even}.
    \end{cases}
    \end{eqnarray*} The general point $[\mathcal{H}_{r}] \in \mathcal M_{\mathbb{F}_e}(r)$ corresponds to a  slope-stable vector bundle.

body_md:
(a) When $e >0$, the fact that $\mathbb{F}_e$ does not support line bundles which are Ulrich w.r.t. $c_1(\mathcal{E}_e) = 3 C_e + b_ef$ is proved in \cite[Thm.\;2.1]{a-c-mr}; however, this fact is also a direct consequence of {\bf Main Theorem}--(a) and Theorem \ref{pullback}. 

For $e=0$  observe that the line bundles $L_1$ and $L_2$ as in {\bf Main Theorem}--(a), which are Ulrich w.r.t. $\xi$ on $X_0$, give rise, by push forward and by Theorem \ref{pullback}, to Ulrich line bundles  w.r.t $c_1(\mathcal{E}_0)=3C_0+b_0 f$ on $\mathbb{F}_0$. Indeed
\begin{eqnarray*}
L_1\otimes \xi^{\vee} = \varphi^{*}\mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_0}(2,-1)\, \, \mbox{and} \,\, L_2\otimes \xi^{\vee} = \varphi^{*}\mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_0}(-1,b_0-1),
\end{eqnarray*}
 thus 
\begin{eqnarray*}
\varphi_{*}(L_1\otimes \xi^{\vee})=\mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_0}(2,-1)\, \, \mbox{and} \,\,\varphi_{*}(L_2\otimes \xi^{\vee})=\mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_0}(-1,b_0-1),
\end{eqnarray*} which give 
\begin{eqnarray*}
\mathcal L_1 := \varphi_{*}(L_1\otimes \xi^{\vee})\otimes \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_0}(c_1(\mathcal{E}_0))=  \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_0}(5,b_0-1) \\
 \mathcal L_2 := \varphi_{*}(L_2\otimes \xi^{\vee})\otimes \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_0}(c_1(\mathcal{E}_0))= \mathcal O_{\mathbb{F}_0}(2,2b_0-1)
\end{eqnarray*}that are the only Ulrich line bundles on $\mathbb{F}_0$ w.r.t. $c_1(\mathcal{E}_e) =3C_0+b_0 f$, according to \cite[Example 2.3]{cas} and \cite[Proposition 4.4]{ant}.


\smallskip

\noindent
(b) As for any rank $r \geqslant 2$ in the case $e=0$, observe that vector bundles $\mathcal{U}_r$ on $X_0$ as in {\bf Main Theorem}--(b) when restricted to a general fibre $F$ of $\varphi: X_0 \to \mathbb{F}_0$ are such that $\mathcal{U}_r|_F \cong \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb P^1}(1)^{\oplus r}$. To see this, one proceeds by induction. By \eqref{extension1}, $L_1|_F \cong \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb P^1}(1) \cong L_2|_F$, thus \linebreak 
$\mathcal{F}_1| _F \in {\rm Ext}^1(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb P^1}(1),\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb P^1}(1))=H^1(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb P^1})=(0)$, hence
$\mathcal{F}_1| _F \cong \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb P^1}(1)^{\oplus 2}$, which is the most balanced splitting.
Since $\mathcal{U}_2=\mathcal{U}$ as in Theorem \ref{prop:rk 2 simple Ulrich vctB e=0;I} 
is a deformation of  $\mathcal{F}_1$ then $\mathcal{U}_2 |_F \cong \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb P^1}(1)^{\oplus 2}$.  Assume by induction, that for some $r \geqslant 3$ one has $\mathcal{U}_{r-1} |_F \cong \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb P^1}(1)^{\oplus r-1}$ for $[\mathcal{U}_{r-1}] \in \mathcal{M}(r-1)$ general.
Then by \eqref{eq:estensioneL}, one has
\begin{eqnarray*}
0 \to \mathcal{U}_{r-1} |_F =\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb P^1}(1)^{\oplus r-1} \to \mathcal{F}_r |_F\to L_{\epsilon_r}|_F=\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb P^1}(1) \to 0
 \end{eqnarray*}
 and, once again, since ${\rm Ext}^1(\mathcal{O}_{\mathbb P^1}(1), \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb P^1}(1)^{\oplus r-1} )=0$ then $\mathcal{F}_r |_F\cong \mathcal{O}_{\mathbb P^1}(1)^{\oplus r}$. 

Thus by \cite[Theorem 6.1]{f-lc-pl}, using the diagram 
 
 \begin{equation*}
    \label{composition}
    \xymatrix@-2ex{
    \tilde{S} \, \, \ar@{^{(}->}[r]^i \ar[rd]_{\varphi'} & X_0\ar[d]^{\varphi} \\
                                      & {\mathbb{F}_0}
    }
\end{equation*}
therein, where $\varphi':   \tilde{S} \to \mathbb{F}_0$ is the blow-up  at $c_2(\mathcal{E}_0)$ points on $\mathbb{F}_0$ and where $\sum E_i$  is the  $\varphi'$-exceptional divisor, one has that $\varphi_*(\mathcal{U}_r \otimes i_*(\mathcal{O}_{\tilde{S}}(\sum E_i)))$ is a rank $r$ vector bundle on $\mathbb{F}_0$ which is Ulrich w.r.t. $c_1(\mathcal{E}_0)=3C_0+b_0 f $. More precisely 
\cite[Proposition 6.2]{f-lc-pl} gives rise to a component of the moduli space of Ulrich bundles of rank $r$ on $\mathbb{F}_0$, which are Ulrich w.r.t.  $c_1(\mathcal{E}_0)=3C_0+b_0 f$, of first Chern class 
\begin{eqnarray*}
c_1(\varphi_*(\mathcal{U}_r \otimes i_*(\mathcal{O}_{\tilde{S}}(\sum E_i)))).
 \end{eqnarray*} On the other hand, if we set $\mathcal{H}_r := \varphi_*(\mathcal{U}_r \otimes i_*(\mathcal{O}_{\tilde{S}}(\sum E_i)))$, 
the one-to-one correspondence in \cite[Proposition 6.2]{f-lc-pl} asserts that $\mathcal{U}_r \cong \xi \otimes \varphi^*(\mathcal{H}_r(-c_1(\mathcal{E}_0)))$. From {\bf Main Theorem}-(b) one knows 
$c_1(\mathcal{U}_r \otimes  \xi^{\vee})$ and, since $c_1(\mathcal{U}_r \otimes  \xi^{\vee}) =  c_1(\mathcal{H}_r(-c_1(\mathcal{E}_0))) =  c_1(\mathcal{H}_r)-r c_1(\mathcal{E}_0)$, it follows that 
$c_1 (\mathcal{H}_r)$ is as stated; pairs $(r, c_1(\mathcal{H}_r))$ are {\em Ulrich admissible pairs} w.r.t. $3C_0+b_0 f$ in the sense of \cite[Def.\;5.1]{ant}.

By  the one-to-one correspondence in \cite[Proposition 6.2]{f-lc-pl} and {\bf Main Theorem}-(b), we have therefore the existence of moduli spaces 
$\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{F}_0}(r)$ of Ulrich bundles on $\mathbb{F}_0$ w.r.t. $ 3 C_0 + b_0 f$, of any rank $r\geqslant 2$, of first Chern class and dimension as stated. 
Moreover since $\mathcal{U}_r \cong \xi \otimes \varphi^*(\mathcal{H}_r(-c_1(\mathcal{E}_0)))$ then
\begin{eqnarray*}
h^j(X_0, \mathcal{U}_r \otimes \mathcal{U}_r^{\vee})&=&h^j(X_0,  \varphi^*(\mathcal{H}_r(-c_1(\mathcal{E}_0)))\otimes \varphi^*(\mathcal{H}_r(-c_1(\mathcal{E}_0)))^{\vee})\\ \nonumber
&=& h^j(X_0,  \varphi^*(\mathcal{H}_r\otimes \mathcal{H}_r^{\vee}))=h^j(\mathbb{F}_0,  \mathcal{H}_r\otimes  \mathcal{H}_r^{\vee}),  
\end{eqnarray*}i.e. $h^2(\mathbb{F}_0,  \mathcal{H}_r\otimes  \mathcal{H}_r^{\vee}) =0$ and $h^0(\mathbb{F}_0,  \mathcal{H}_r\otimes  \mathcal{H}_r^{\vee}) =1$, 
namely the component  $\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{F}_0}(r)$ is also generically smooth and its general point $[\mathcal{H}_r] \in  \mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{F}_0}(r)$ corresponds to a simple bundle. 

It is also clear that $\mathcal{H}_r$ is slope-stable w.r.t. $3 C_0 + b_0f$: if not, by the one-to-one correspondence given by \cite[Proposition 6.2]{f-lc-pl}, any destabilizing rank-$k$ 
Ulrich sub-bundle $\mathcal D_k$ of $ \mathcal \mathcal{H}_r$ general, for some $1 \leqslant k \leqslant r-1$, would give rise to a rank-$k$ 
vector bundle $\xi \otimes \varphi^*(\mathcal D_k(- c_1 (\mathcal E_0))$ which is Ulrich on $X_0$ w.r.t. $\xi$, by Theorem \ref{pullback}, and which would be a 
destabilizing sub-bundle on $\mathcal{U}_r$ general in $\mathcal M(r)$ on $X_0$, contradicting {\bf Main Theorem}--(b).  

When $r=2,3$, the previous arguments are in accordance with \cite[Prop.\;6.4]{ant}, for the polarization $3C_0+b_0 f$, and $c_1$ as stated.


\smallskip

\noindent
(c) Similar arguments as in (b), but for the case for $e>0$, are obtained by using {\bf Main Theorem}--(c), Theorem \ref{pullback} and the one-to-one correspondence in \cite[Proposition 6.2]{f-lc-pl}.
